fact: The model catalog is generated: people edit catalog JSON under packages/ai/model-registry/catalog, and pnpm sync:models compiles registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and two Rust mirrors.
Never hand-edit packages/contracts/types/src/models.json; a model ID may be a literal only in the catalog, enforced by check:model-id-literals and a Rust guard.
The generated registry read on 2026-11-24 holds 394 models, 463 routes, 38 harnesses and 15 runtime profiles; 389 models are live.
Every model has one 22-name capability vocabulary; null means unverified and is treated as not offered.
Capabilities are split into intrinsic (model) and route-dependent (needs route or AGI harness); route-dependent ones are never sufficient alone.
model-families.json has 28 family slots; each has active, previous, fallbackChain (limit 3), history and snapshots; defaults point at family:<provider>/<family>.

13 of 28 family slots are seeded (no gate run); 8 active promotion records say the eval gate was not run (openai gpt-frontier, gpt-balanced, gpt-fast, gpt-image; anthropic (model name), (model name); google (model name), gemini-flash-image).
Family fallback chains are empty for 27 of 28 slots and hold one entry in the other, though the policy limit is 3; recovery from a bad promotion is mostly rollback to the previous model.
Promote or roll back a family with pnpm models:families:promote or :rollback --slot <id> --apply; inspect with pnpm models:families.

Auto aliases are auto (default), auto-economy, auto-balanced, auto-premium; auto computes the band per task, and resolveRoutingLane clamps it by tierMaximumProfiles (free/basic economy, pro balanced, max/enterprise/byok premium) after normalizeTier; unknown tiers default to economy.

tierMaximumProfiles and tierAllowedSlots each have six keys (free, basic, pro, max, enterprise, byok); max_15x, team and team_premium rely on normalizeTier. Free's allowed slots are free_workhorse, free_workhorse_fast, fast_anthropic.
The auto alias has tierPolicy minTier basic while Free has an economy band and three allowed slots; the reconciliation is not traced.
Auto policy has 47 slots, 11 task types and 12 task families.
Privacy and policy rules are hard admission filters applied before ranking: trust mode, zero data retention, no-training, region, US-only, developer country, workspace policy.
Route ranking order: healthy, credentialed, lower observed penalty, lower expected cost, model default route, route id; a warm-cache route is kept unless it costs over 1.25 times the cheapest.
The task-family stage orders only the already-admitted set by expected cost among candidates meeting a quality floor; it is a permutation, with kill switch AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE.
Auto keeps the conversation's current model for cache continuity while it stays eligible and costs at most 2 times the cheapest floor-meeting candidate.

A named model is served as 'explicit'; if it is ineligible the resolver returns explicit_model_ineligible, unless fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch is set (mobile and Chrome set it, web exact selection clears it).
Billing follows the model's official price while cost follows the served route, so a cheaper host does not change what the user pays.
Plan display names: Local Mode, Local Mode + BYOK, Free, Basic, Premium (id pro), Max, Ultra (id max_15x), Team, Team Premium, Enterprise.

Local Mode (plan id `local-only`) is priced at 0 USD and is listed for web, desktop and mobile in the plan table only; Local is offered on Mobile, CLI, VS Code and the retained Tauri build, not on web or the public Electron Desktop. It has maxSandboxes 0, maxScheduledTasks 0 and codeHarnessDailyCeilingCents 0; so sandboxes, scheduled tasks and the cloud code harness are off.
The retained Tauri desktop code (not the public Electron Desktop) builds a local device account with plan local-only, name Local Mode and subscriptionStatus none.
Local needs no account: Mobile allows signed-out use after an on-device age confirmation and onboarding; the CLI and VS Code need no account; the public Electron Desktop chat has no Local mode.
Mobile on-device model files are downloaded from huggingface.co with pinned SHA-256 hashes and sizes, so first use needs an outside service.
Free may name only economy models marked minTier free; pro adds pro models; max and enterprise add flagships.
Switching provider inside one conversation is allowed only for max, max_15x, team_premium and enterprise.
Web warns before a model switch: 'Switch to <model>?' with findings for no images, no tools or context overflow, and a Switch anyway button.
VS Code shows a modal listing losses (no tools, no images, smaller context) before switching, with a Switch anyway choice.
Chrome browser actions fail with '<model> does not support browser tools, screenshots, and streaming.' when the chosen model lacks tools, vision or streaming; Auto picks a capable model instead.
The CLI drops tools for a local model that does not advertise tool support and prints a notice that the turn runs without tools.
Mobile maps unavailable routing codes to fixed messages, for example 'No available AGI Cloud model supports this request. Try a different model or remove the attachment.'
The Rust crate agiworkforce-model-registry holds a second resolver (resolve_auto_route) over the same generated policy; both replay one conformance fixture, and which is canonical is undecided.
Free Auto, task-family stage, canary, shadow, health ranking and preferSlots are TypeScript-only; the Rust resolver has no counterpart.
Runtime profiles: local profiles for desktop, mobile and CLI are partial; mobile on_device lists zero harnesses; desktop local lists ollama and lmstudio harnesses; VS Code BYOK and local are unwired.
Mobile on-device models come from a separate catalog (packages/platform/local-llm) with five capability flags, not the registry vocabulary.
Named routing profiles (Instant, High, Code, Research) define quality, cost and latency weights, but weightedScore is not called by resolveAutoRoute.
Every routing decision is traced in table routing_decision_traces (migration 0212) and compared hourly by /api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout.
Every vendor adapter implements one interface, ProviderAdapter, with catalog() and stream(req, signal); apps depend on it, not on vendor SDKs.

There are 17 leaf provider packages plus a factory: anthropic, deepseek, google, groq, lmstudio, minimax, moonshot, nvidia, ollama, openai, openrouter, perplexity, qwen, vercel-gateway, workers-ai, xai, zhipu.
The factory has 18 adapter ids, including a generic openai_compat id used for protocol routes and gateways. It holds no keys.
Adapters do not retry. Retry runs at the stream-start seam in web, and rotation runs above it in managed-failover.ts.
Same-route retry allows 2 attempts for most retryable classes and 3 for server_overload; auth and context_overflow are never retried on the same route.
Timeouts: turn first-token budget 40 s, per-provider first-token deadline 25 s, function limit 300 s, TS stream idle default 90 s, CLI stream idle 300 s.

Rotation categories: connection, server_error, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, api_timeout, rate_limit, quota_exhausted, empty_response, unsupported_input. Never rotated: billing_exhausted, safety, content_blocked.
Only Auto may switch models during failover; a named model rotates only across routes of the same model.
Once a provider has minted tool-call ids in a turn (step 2 onward) the turn stays on that provider.
Billing exhaustion is classified separately from auth so unfunded accounts do not rotate onto another paid provider; one Auto-only exception exists.
Gateway routes are declarative (gateways.json plus a harness gatewayId) and off unless AGI_ROUTING_GATEWAY_ROUTES=1; the flag is enforced at admission and at dispatch.
Nine gateway definitions exist in the catalog; openrouter_via_gateway is deliberately not wired.
Base URL overrides are accepted only for allowlisted hosts, https only (http for localhost and 127.0.0.1); the allowlist is a static list plus registry-declared hosts.
Web keeps keys in environment variables and builds adapters server-side; unconfigured providers throw ProviderConfigurationError naming the variable.
Perplexity is the search-grounded chat provider (citations on the last chunk), and the only web-search provider entry is Perplexity Search.
Image generation uses OpenAI and Google by direct fetch, defaulting to Google if its key exists, else OpenAI; a Stability branch exists but throws unsupported.
Speech to text and text to speech are OpenAI by direct fetch; the transcription route requires the voice_transcription slot to resolve to an OpenAI model.
Rust engine agiworkforce-llm speaks five dialects (Anthropic, Gemini, OllamaNative, OpenAiResponses, OpenAiCompat), never reads keys itself, and redacts auth in Debug output.
The CLI hard-codes endpoint URLs for Anthropic, Gemini and pre-registered OpenAI-compatible providers in Rust.
Mobile on-device inference uses @agiworkforce/local-llm with llama.rn, ExecuTorch and system models, not the TS provider packages.

Mobile cloud models are gated by a cloudUnlocked flag and the subscription tier (canAccessCloudModelForTier); a cloud model is 'locked' otherwise. Local models are not gated by these checks. This is mobile-side list logic, separate from web's server-side canAccessModel.

Mobile also lists provider-funded Free quota chat models: surface cloud_managed, runtimeLabel 'Provider-funded Free', described as promotional quota, shown only when cloud is unlocked. They are cloud calls, not on-device.
Runtime profiles mark vscode/byok-chat and vscode/local-chat unwired, and the desktop, mobile and CLI local profiles partial.
A mistral harness is declared in the registry but names a nonexistent package, and web ADAPTER_PROVIDERS has no mistral entry.
Apps may not import provider leaf internals; multi-provider code uses the factory. Routing decisions belong to packages/ai/routing.

fact: Managed billing debits the model's official price while recording the served route's price as cost, so a cheaper host never changes what the user pays.

The Chrome extension imports only ThinkingTagSplitter from provider-protocol, in three files; it declares provider-runtime as a dependency but no source import was found. The VS Code extension runs a per-workspace local runtime process instead of calling providers.
The provider-runtime header names apps/mobile and apps/extension as consumers of the error taxonomy, but both only declare the dependency in package.json and neither imports it in source.
Public Desktop (Electron) refuses every local-inference command with unsupported-platform and reports localModels false; its chat is Cloud-only.
The six refused commands are local_model_servers, local_model_list, local_chat_start, local_chat_cancel, local_model_settings_read and local_model_settings_write.
Desktop coding sessions run the bundled CLI, which can use a local model; this is the only way local models reach public Desktop.
Mobile has four local runtime names: foundation_models (Apple), aicore (Google), executorch, and llama_rn, grouped into tiers 1, 2 and 3.
ExecuTorch (tier 2) needs at least 3500 MB RAM, or unknown RAM with the module present; llama.rn (tier 3) is always marked available.
Four catalog entries ship on Mobile v1 (default text, lite text, Apple system model, Google system model); vision entries are not shippable.
The on-device model catalog is a hand-written TypeScript list, not the generated model catalog.
Mobile model downloads come from Hugging Face over HTTPS; GGUF files are SHA-256 verified, resumable, Wi-Fi only by default, and need free disk of file size plus 256 MB.
ExecuTorch downloads are fetched by the react-native-executorch resource fetcher; the app records sha256 null for them, so it does not verify a checksum itself.

Model files are stored under documents/models/<id>/model.gguf and documents/react-native-executorch/, excluded from backup; installs are recorded in the installed_models table of the on-device encrypted SQLite database.
Mobile Local chat does not require sign-in: routing sends a signed-out user to the app after the age gate and onboarding, and the Local send branch has no auth check.
The age gate runs before everything on Mobile including Local Mode, and the answer is held on the device.
Mobile Local turns carry no plan, entitlement or consent check; those calls are in the cloud branch only.
A Mobile Local chat refuses cloud models and a cloud chat refuses local models, with an error asking for a separate chat.
Mobile Local branch returns before tools, web search, connectors and sync; account switches show 'Cloud only'; image/video generation and live voice need cloud.
On Mobile Local, image attachments become on-device OCR text only; the model cannot see pixels.

The mobile egress guard's message describes Local Mode as 'on-device + BYOK only', although Mobile has no own-key mode. The guard throws EgressBlockedError (EGRESS_BLOCKED_LOCAL_MODE) for our managed-cloud hosts before any network I/O, except for an allow list.

In Mobile Local mode the guard still allows signed-in account controls to AGI servers: terms acceptance, the age check that opens Cloud, account deletion status, scheduling and cancellation, the deletion identity check, and data export. The guard comment says none carries chat content. It also allows a user-sent content report, withdrawal controls, and any non-AGI host (a boundary gap, since Mobile has no own-key mode; the guard comment's 'BYOK direct-to-provider' is stale).
Local Mobile sessions are labelled local_device storage with syncEligible false; cloud sync is queued only in cloud mode.
The CLI supports exactly two local runtimes, Ollama (default http://localhost:11434) and LM Studio (default http://localhost:1234/v1); it discovers models but does not download them.
The CLI Local first run needs no account and never shows cloud login; README states Local mode and BYOK need no plan.
CLI Local sessions refuse cloud calls (CloudClient::admit allows Managed only), and the device heartbeat only runs for Managed, so Local does not report to AGI servers.
VS Code has no model runtime of its own; it asks the CLI app-server for local models and shows an 'On this device' group; an AGI Cloud account is not required for Local.
VS Code never swaps a Local default model for a cloud model; Code Review, Suggest Terminal Command and inline completions run only on AGI Cloud and send nothing when a Local model is selected.

The Chrome extension has no local inference. Its device heartbeat to the cloud bridge always sends capabilities.localModels false, and the only 'ollama' and 'lmstudio' strings in its side panel are provider icon ids.
Web has local-chat UI and client code gated to a host whose shell is tauri; no handler for the six local-inference commands was found in Rust or Electron, so the path appears to have no backend.
The Web composer hides the Local models row for Free-plan users (!freePlan && localModels.available), a plan-linked rule in a path that is not reachable on Electron.
The shared local-inference contract requires loopback base URLs, refuses attachments, and hides models under 1B parameters.
Public marketing says Local runs in the CLI with Ollama and LM Studio, costs $0 and needs no account.
Requirement: Local mode needs no AGI account, keeps storage local, makes no hidden cloud call and fails closed.

One shared, platform-free list of our-cloud hosts (web domain, Vercel, Neon, four Clerk domains) is the single source for every device guard. Matching is suffix-based, case-insensitive and trailing-dot tolerant.
BYOK provider hosts are deliberately not on the our-cloud list, so direct own-key calls are never blocked.

The mobile guard treats Cloud as open only when appMode is cloud and the signed-in account's provider consent is current. Otherwise any our-cloud host throws EgressBlockedError before network I/O. It fails closed when mode, consent or withdrawal state cannot be read.
In mobile Local mode only three classes of request reach our servers: signed-in account controls, withdrawal controls, and one content report the person sends with its own Send tap.

The desktop renderer egress guard fails open for a target whose host cannot be parsed: extractHost returns null on a parse error and the guard throws only for a non-null host on the our-cloud list. A relative-path request in private mode is not blocked by this guard.

The mobile consent alert is titled 'Share with AI providers?' and names every provider the app can route to. Consent is stored per account with the provider ids covered, and is not current if a new provider has been added or a withdrawal is in progress.

Every write to the mobile app mode passes one admission function, so the mode cannot be Cloud without current consent. Declining keeps Local. Withdrawal returns to Local, pauses schedules and runs, and turns off Ask from Siri.

A mobile conversation keeps its mode. A Local chat refuses Cloud models and a Cloud chat refuses local models; there is no in-app continuation from Local to Cloud. The only crossing is a manual, confirmed copy of selected chats' text, done in Cloud mode.
Mobile has no own-key mode. The remote-chat gate accepts a byokKeys flag and never consults it.
The mobile remote-chat gate has a v1LocalOnly build flag; when set, Cloud is blocked without an explicit unlock. No released build sets it.
Mobile Local chat needs no AGI account or plan on its path; the router lets a signed-out user into the app after onboarding and an on-device age confirmation.

The public Electron Desktop shell refuses every local-inference command with 'unsupported-platform'. The code names decision D-2026-09-15-04 (desktop chat is Cloud-only) as the reason, and says local coding sessions reach local models through the bundled CLI. This conflicts with the stated product requirement that desktop local inference is free.
The desktop renderer guard reads the privacy mode; anything not 'managed', or an exception while reading it, counts as private. A script fails any renderer file that calls fetch directly.

The shared preview builder redacts secrets, hashes the payload, sets consentRequired true and marks the preview blocked when findings exist and blockOnFindings is on (default on). The Tauri own-key fork passes blockOnFindings false and no provider label; the folder-to-Cloud sheet passes true and the label 'AGI Managed Cloud'.

On web, sending from a Local chat to a direct own-key model opens a consent dialog instead of sending, and regenerate is refused. The dialog shows 'Local to Direct BYOK' with the provider name and says the Local thread is unchanged.

The Tauri Rust command llm_create_byok_fork stores only the already-approved messages as a new own-key conversation and leaves the Local conversation untouched; it does not itself check that consent was given.

The server mode contract defines Local as device storage, no key, fallback refuse; own key as user-provider storage, user key, same-boundary fallback; managed as managed-cloud storage, platform key, sync across devices.
refuseTrustTransition (loosening a mode needs approval) is exported but no product file calls it; only a support-claims file names it.

evaluateProviderEgress refuses a provider call that carries a secret, uses a platform key under an own-key conversation, or uses an unapproved or boundary-leaving fallback; every decision produces an audit event. Its only direct product caller is buildProviderEgressGateResponse in managed-compute-gate.ts, which three product files use (artifact completion, experiential-free completions route, free-quota turn).

Code plan tiers are free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise (plus local-only and byok at zero price). Labels shown to people: basic is Basic, pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra. PAID_TIERS means basic and above; PRO_TIERS means pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise.

Plan capabilities: chat, tools, projects, memory, skills and sync are in every tier from free; connectors and remote control are PAID_TIERS; AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API and developer surfaces are PRO_TIERS; video only max_15x and enterprise.

Which plan capability a Cloud chat needs depends on the calling app: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome need managed_chat (all tiers from free); CLI and VS Code need developer_surfaces (PRO_TIERS); the open API needs managed_api. A token bound to no app gets none. So a Free or Basic account gets Cloud chat on four apps and not on CLI or VS Code: not one uniform subscription check.

Plan limits by tier: Free has 5 projects, 5 uploads per day, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 2 sandboxes, 0 scheduled tasks and no coding-agent budget; Basic has 3 scheduled tasks and 5 sandboxes; Premium (pro) has 5 scheduled tasks and 10 sandboxes. local-only and byok tiers have 0 sandboxes and 0 scheduled tasks.

AGI Code (cloud coding) is included when a plan has both a sandbox allowance and a daily coding-agent budget above zero, which starts at Basic. This differs from the PRO_TIERS rule for CLI and VS Code Cloud models.
Every product tier allows web search and voice. Free has no manual model selection, no image or video generation, and 10 voice minutes per month.
The tier policy declares which provider surfaces each tier may use (Free: managed cloud only), but no code reads that field, so own-key use is not blocked by it.

Mobile live voice, web search, deep research, cloud code execution and Cloud-side memory are reached only in the Cloud branch of the send path. Turn-based speech capture on mobile requires an on-device recognizer and refuses otherwise.
Mobile Cloud sync, product analytics and Cloud memory run only in Cloud mode; the mobile sync engine also needs an account epoch.

The CLI discovers local models on loopback addresses (Ollama and LM Studio defaults) and never gates local or own-key models by plan; it hides every managed model from Free, Basic and own-key accounts.

VS Code supports Local through the CLI app-server (local model list for Ollama and LM Studio) and own key through the provider sign-in command that runs the CLI login. Neither needs an AGI account or plan; only Cloud models need a Premium-or-higher plan. The harness catalog marks vscode/local-chat and vscode/byok-chat as unwired, which lags the implementation.
CI runs check:trust-boundaries (seven surface proofs plus a no-remote-crash-reporting check on the Tauri crate) and check:rust-egress-boundary. This pass ran none of them.

The harness catalog marks mobile Local, desktop Local and CLI Local as partial, marks VS Code Local and own key as unwired (a flag that lags the extension, which supports both through the CLI), and records Cloud as implemented on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
Plan tiers are local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; pro is shown as Premium and max_15x as Ultra.

The plan catalog marks every plan, including local-only and byok, selectable on web, desktop and mobile. This is visibility in the plan table, not mode support: Local is offered only on Mobile, CLI, VS Code and the retained Tauri build.

Mode support by app: mobile has Local and Cloud (no BYOK); web is Cloud only; public Desktop chat is Cloud only and rejects local-inference commands; Chrome is Cloud only; CLI and VS Code support subscription, BYOK and local models.
local-only and byok get zero managed usage in every window, are absent from the cloud chat capability tiers (managed chat, cloud sync, projects denied), and have zero sandboxes and scheduled tasks.
Enterprise has unlimited managed usage: unlimited true with zero window numbers, plan credit allowance Infinity, and an uncapped ledger allocation constant.
The CLI has its own Byok tier whose enforcement is left to the user, so local and BYOK CLI use is not gated by the account tier.

Local needs no account: a signed-out Mobile user passes the on-device age confirmation, then onboarding and the app; CLI and VS Code need no account for Local; Electron Desktop chat has no Local mode. In Mobile Local mode the egress guard blocks managed-cloud hosts except account controls, withdrawal controls and a user-sent content report; sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mode.
Monthly USD prices: Basic 7, Premium 20, Max 100, Ultra 200, Team 25 per seat, Team Premium 125 per seat; Enterprise is contract priced.
1 credit equals $0.005 of provider cost (5,000 microUSD); credits are the only usage unit shown to customers.

A top-up buys 50 credits per $1 paid (TOP_UP_UNITS_PER_USD) while a credit is $0.005 of provider cost (200 credits per $1 of cost, CREDITS_PER_USD). The two constants are kept separate and not reconciled; whether the gap is a deliberate markup or a defect is not established. Minimum $20, maximum $1,000, $2,000 a day; auto-reload threshold 100 to 100,000 credits.

Per-plan credit windows (5-hour / weekly / monthly): Free 200/1,500/2,000; Basic 10/100/400; Premium 50/500/2,000; Max 250/2,500/10,000; Ultra none/5,000/20,000; Team 50/500/2,000 per seat; Team Premium 250/2,500/10,000 per seat.
Ultra (max_15x) has no 5-hour cap (null); a zero cap means zero allowed usage.
Flagship-model usage is capped at 30% of the weekly allowance on Premium, Max, Ultra and per-seat team plans; Basic and Free have no flagship cap.
The 5-hour and weekly windows are rolling sums over the last 5 and 168 hours of credit_transactions deductions; rows tagged is_overage are excluded.
The monthly window follows the subscription billing period; periods over 45 days (yearly) are cut into monthly slices anchored to the start date.
Entitlement resolves in one function: own entitled paid row, then team seat, then own lapsed or free row, then none.
Only active and trialing statuses are entitled; any other status collapses the effective plan to free. Enterprise also tolerates past_due and unpaid unless collection is read-only.

Apps ask for entitlement through GET /api/me, which returns plan, effective_tier, subscription_source, billing_owner, feature flags and a four-layer capability handshake (model, tier, surface, settings).

Capabilities by tier: connectors and Remote Control from Basic; AGI Work, Deep Research, images, managed API, developer surfaces from Premium; video only Ultra and Enterprise; team admin on team plans and Enterprise.
Every managed turn reserves usage through a per-user database function and is refused with a typed decision (402 or 429 codes) or 503 billing_unavailable when billing cannot answer.
Funding order is plan windows, then bonus credits, then purchased credits only when usage credits are on; a turn that crosses a cap finishes on the plan.

Free accounts are admitted through a separate Free ledger (free_daily_usage_reservations and website_auto_economy_trial_usage); the paid ledger helpers give Free a zero budget. Free product limits include 5 projects, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 0 scheduled tasks, 5 daily attachment uploads and 2 sandboxes.

Checkout is gated: an account without a live paid subscription needs billing.upgrades_open on (or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1) or any beta_redemptions row; otherwise POST /api/checkout returns 403 with the waitlist code. The flag reads closed on any error.

A subscription has one billing owner. A malformed Stripe subscription id or ids from more than one channel read as unverified and fail closed. With no store id and no Stripe subscription id: free tier reads none; a valid Stripe customer id reads stripe; otherwise a non-free tier reads manual. Store rows expire 3 days after paid-through.

The Stripe webhook rate-limits and verifies the signature, dedupes by event id (200 if done, 503 with Retry-After 10 if still processing), runs the handler and idempotency mark in one transaction, and returns 500 on failure so Stripe retries.
Mobile v1 sells nothing: storePurchases.json has nativePurchases false, compiled per build; mobile only refreshes the tier in cloud mode.
CLI and VS Code cache the account tier for 300 seconds; the CLI keeps a higher cached tier over a lower fetched one and times out the fetch at 3 seconds.
Team seat entitlement comes from the organization owner's subscription, limited by join-order rank within licensed_seats; /api/me reports subscription_source manual for seat holders.
The offline licensing verifier (TypeScript package and Rust crate) is not wired into any app runtime.
Catalog versions 1 to 4 all map to the same allowance table; a subscription records the version it was sold under.
No plan in the catalog sets trialDays, so trials come only from referrals.
Access codes open acquisition only and grant no plan or trial.

Apps with their own plan logic include the CLI tier enum, the VS Code alias map and mobile direct free comparisons. The retained Tauri code (not the public Desktop) derives subscription status locally and uses a free/basic/hobby budget-plan routing hint, which is not an entitlement check.
The identity provider is Clerk by default, selected through a port; `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` can name another provider but only `clerk` is implemented.
Web proxy returns 503 for session routes if the authorized-party allowlist cannot be resolved, instead of authenticating without the origin check.

A signed-out visitor to a protected product route is redirected to /login with redirectTo, but /chat is exempt from the cookie check. Guest Cloud chat on /chat exists only while the guest.chat feature flag is on; web has no Local mode.
Desktop sign-in uses a PKCE-like hand-off: the shell keeps a random verifier in memory, sends its SHA-256 challenge to the browser, and redeems a one-time code with the verifier.
The desktop pending attempt lives 10 minutes; the server grant and the sign-in ticket live 60 seconds; the grant is stored only as a hash.
The desktop deep link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud and the host is sign-in.
Redeem is accepted only in a desktop host that reports browser sign-in support, so a grant opened in an ordinary browser fails.
CLI, VS Code and (in the Tauri build) desktop link through an RFC 8628 device grant: code issued with 900 s life and 5 s poll interval, approved on /auth/device, exchanged at /api/auth/device/token.
Device access tokens are web-signed JWTs valid 7 days; refresh tokens are 32 random bytes stored as SHA-256 hashes and valid 30 days, rotated on use.
A replayed refresh token marks its whole family compromised and revokes it.
Device approval is refused for developer-token callers, when the account has device sign-in switched off, when Terms need acceptance, or when no current 18-and-over decision exists.
Mobile Cloud calls send the Clerk session token as Bearer plus a Clerk-template surface proof in a separate header; the server admits a native token only with a matching proof.
Mobile root routing requires a device-level age gate before any screen, then lets signed-out users stay in the app; sign-in screens open only on request or when a ended session is owed.
The Chrome extension reuses the web session through Clerk syncHost, requires a token whose azp equals the extension origin, and opens /sign-in which redirects to /login.

The minimum account age is 18 on every surface and in every region. The mobile gate has a per-region table (India, Brazil, default) in which every entry is 18, and it floors each threshold at ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE. The server stores only outcome, minimum age, method and time, never the age.
An age decision made under a lower minimum no longer counts and the person is asked again; an ineligible outcome stands.

Server-side 18-and-over enforcement covers login-complete, device grant, product page layouts, LLM chat, embeddings, transcription, speech, live voice, image and video generation and mobile intents, not every API route.
Sign out everywhere is DELETE /api/settings/sessions: it needs CSRF and a step-up proof, ends all other provider sessions, then the current one, and revokes every device refresh credential.

Product session cap is measured from session creation, on top of the provider's idle expiry. SESSION_ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME_HOURS is an environment setting that defaults to 720 hours (30 days) when unset or invalid.

A user-selectable idle sign-out (session_timeout in Security settings) is a browser-side timer in useSessionTimeout that the server never reads and mobile does not enforce. The checked-in hook falls back to 60 minutes when no value is stored; 70-qa/start-here/where-things-stand.md records the fixed behaviour as off unless the person picks a limit, so the shipped default is not established.
The provider-side session length is not in the repository.
evidence: apps/web/lib/auth/session-policy.ts comment says the provider's expiry renews on use

fact: Linked devices are rows in device_registrations created by POST /api/devices/heartbeat and managed through /api/settings/devices.
CLI credentials sit in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) or an owner-only file when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1; VS Code uses SecretStorage.
apps/cli/src/trust/identity.rs is workspace identity for trust grants (git remote key), not account sign-in.
CLI logout posts to /api/auth/logout, which revokes the token id and the whole session family, or the family named by a refresh token.
Enabled web sign-in providers come from AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS among google, github, microsoft, apple; default google and github.
Sign-in, device approval and token issue do not check a plan; plan gating happens after identity.

The server resolves a request's workspace from the x-agi-organization-id header (value 'personal' means Personal), else a cached selection, else the saved user setting joined to an active membership.
A header naming an organization where the caller has no active membership is refused with 403; a malformed selector gives 400; a failed lookup gives 503.
User queries run as the NOLOGIN, NOBYPASSRLS role app_rls, with request.jwt.claim.sub and request.jwt.claim.org_id set per transaction.
getNeonDb() is the owner connection that bypasses RLS; code using it over user-owned tables must be on a ratcheting allowlist (78 entries, none marked pending).
Personal (organization_id NULL) and each organization are mutually exclusive scopes for content rows; an admin sees others' rows only in the active organization, never personal rows.
The latest app_row_is_visible (migration 0272) shows the owner their row in the active workspace only while an active member, and shows other members' org rows only to holders of content.govern.
Only membership status 'active' carries access; invited, suspended and deprovisioned memberships yield no permissions and no org role.
Built-in roles are primary_owner, owner, admin, member, viewer; permissions are a union of the membership role, extra roles and SCIM directory-group roles.
organization_members.role 'owner' is the single Primary Owner; only it can transfer ownership, delete the workspace, or manage the billing contract, enforced by a check constraint on role rows.
evaluateAuthorization runs five ordered stages (membership, entitlement, permission, policy, rollout); the first refusal wins and Personal scope is allowed outright.
A role grant cannot give permissions the granter lacks; this is enforced in RLS WITH CHECK and in TypeScript.
Workspace routes resolve a caller through a per-route, per-method permission table; routes absent from it are closed to workspace API keys (prefix agiadm_).
Team administration needs plan capability team_admin (team, team_premium, enterprise); SSO, SCIM and admin controls need enterprise_controls (enterprise).

A shared project is readable by its owner, or by a member whose coalesce(per-member grant, default_access) is read or write; 'none' hides it. Write needs an explicit per-member grant and a role that still holds content.share.
A project's owner can share it and choose who opens it if their role holds content.share; others need sharing.manage.
Conversation shares have visibility 'public' (anyone with the 24-char token until expiry) or 'organization' (members with a grant row); only the share's owner changes it.

Removing a member deletes the membership, clears the cached selection, then revokes this workspace's sessions, device tokens, mobile intent tokens, API keys and shared connectors for that (user, organization) pair; step failures are reported, not thrown.
Invitations last 7 days and can be resent at most 10 times; invitable roles are admin, member, viewer.
A Primary Owner cannot leave without naming an active, entitled successor; a sole owner cannot leave and must delete the workspace.
Platform operators are user ids in an environment allowlist (AGI_PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS); org admins never qualify; non-operators and device tokens get 404; an unset list denies all.
Operator access to customer content goes through support access grants with scopes and a hash-chained trail that also records refused reads.
check:db-isolation keeps a workspace-scope baseline of 18 files that still read Personal and every organization together; the guard's comment calls each a real leak.
Guards check that every membership-ending path revokes credentials and that unattended work re-checks owner membership; both keep baselines that may only shrink.
withUser() decodes the token subject without checking its signature and throws unless the adapter was built with unsafeAllowUnverifiedJwtSubject; the web code verifies tokens first.
Mobile switches workspace via PUT /api/settings/organization/active and reloads chats; the CLI caches the effective workspace policy hourly in a sealed file, valid up to 7 days.
No document in the project records a live run of the RLS probe or the guards; this page's author ran nothing.
Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud.
The public Desktop (Electron) shows the hosted web app, so it inherits the web authorization path.
The cloud schema is 425 contiguous numbered SQL files, 0001 to 0425, in apps/web/db/neon, and filenames must match NNNN_lower_snake_case.sql.
The repository records production as applied through migration 425 on 2026-11-21. Draft headers do not show deployment state.

The runner applies each pending file in its own transaction with lock_timeout 10s and statement_timeout 120s, records a SHA-256 checksum in public.schema_migrations, and holds a session advisory lock.

Commands are inventory, status, apply, verify, baseline, record, deployments. Production mutation needs --confirm-production; local target refuses non-local hosts; apply and baseline swap a -pooler host for the direct host.

An applied migration must never be edited: its checksum is in the ledger and the deploy gate refuses drift. A comment-only edit to 0087 caused a refused promotion with nine migrations queued on 2026-08-24.

Every migration from 0097 on needs a down/NNNN_name.down.sql that opens with BEGIN, ends with COMMIT, names every object touched, and deletes its own ledger row (329 reversal files exist for 0097-0425).

The migration guard rejects column or table renames, NOT NULL columns without a default, add and drop of columns on one table in one file, unmarked destructive statements, blanket GRANT on all tables, and mixed transaction control. Frozen baseline sets name older exceptions.

Row isolation uses a non-bypass role app_rls and transaction-local settings for user id and organization id; policies call current_app_user_id() and current_app_org_id(), which return NULL when unset so access fails closed.
organization_id NULL means a personal row; non-NULL means workspace-owned, visible to the owner and to workspace owners and admins of the active workspace.

The 0037 header says RLS is dormant on the live path; the code now routes request handlers through getUserScopedDb (about 810 files import rls-db). getNeonDb() remains an owner-role handle for crons, webhooks and erasure, and check:rls-boundary allowlists 78 files that use it.
Chats are web_conversations and web_messages (messages cascade from the conversation); server_version from one sequence is the sync cursor; GET and POST /api/chat/sync serve pull and push.
Soft-deleted conversations, messages, artifacts, projects, project knowledge files and media assets are restorable for 30 days, then purged by a daily cron.
Temporary chats are purged 30 days after creation, skipping rows under legal hold.
Account deletion has a 24-hour cancellation window; erasure runs from a daily cron after the deadline. Workspace deletion has a 14-day cooling period.

Erasure inventories: USER_SCOPED_TABLES (hard delete), ANONYMIZED_USER_COLUMNS (content_reports, organization_usage_ledger, project_knowledge_files.added_by_user_id, slack_installations, provider_cost_events, cogs_adjustments, billing_disputes), UNDELETED_USER_TABLES (each with a reason).
RETENTION_MATRIX.md is generated from the erasure lists and retention rules; it lists 246 tables, 7 object stores and 3 caches, and a test fails if it drifts from the code.

Age limits: usage_events minimised at 180 days and purged at 730; credit_transactions minimised at 730 and purged at 2,922 days; credit_settlement_jobs purged at 90 days after completion; security_audit_logs at 90 days.
One credit is 5,000 microUSD. The 0182 migration header says 20,000, which is wrong.

Plan tier ids and labels: free, basic, pro (Premium), max, max_15x (Ultra), team, team_premium, enterprise, plus local-only and byok. In the database, subscriptions.plan_tier was last widened in 0074 and has no team_premium; team_premium is a seat type on Team.

Mobile Local data: a SQLCipher database (agi_mobile.db, user_version 5) keyed from the keychain this-device-only, plus an encrypted MMKV store. Chat messages persist in MMKV; the SQLite conversations and messages tables have only readers.
Public Desktop (Electron) keeps no conversation database. It keeps JSON state in a folder named 'AGI Cloud' and measures sessions in the CLI home.
The retained Tauri desktop build has a SQLCipher database at schema version 89, with a random 256-bit key in the OS credential store, and it refuses a database newer than the app.

CLI sessions are JSONL files under managed_sessions in the CLI home (default ~/.agiworkforce, override AGIWORKFORCE_HOME), with metadata JSON beside them and atomic writes under a directory lock; the CLI no longer uses SQLite for sessions.
The CLI pushes managed-mode sessions to /api/chat/sync; a Local or BYOK session is refused by the client. The module comment in sessions.rs claiming no consumer chat sync is outdated.
Production deploy only runs db:migrate verify; CI applies the chain twice, then verifies and runs an RLS probe.
Recovery is Neon point-in-time branching; there is no separate dump schedule, and the project's retained history window is not recorded in the repository.
143 applied migrations still carry a 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' header; headers are not deployment state.
The legacy tables conversations, messages and chat_messages (0077) are exported and erased but no writer was found in apps/web app or lib.

fact: The developer gateway base is /api/llm/v1 and is OpenAI-compatible; an alias host maps five /v1 paths plus /health.
Three API key scopes exist: models:read, inference:write, usage:read; a key with no scopes gets all three.
Embeddings accepts a session token only; an API key is refused because the route declares no scope.
Chat completions is limited twice: 1500 per minute per IP before auth, then 30 per minute per user, both fail closed.
Other limits per minute: models 100 (key default, fail open), credits balance 60 (open), transcriptions 20 (closed), embeddings 60 (open, key chat-conversation).
API-key requests are not verified locally by the limiter, so their bucket is the client IP, except chat completions which passes user:<id>.
A 429 body has error.code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, retry_after_seconds, reset_at and a rateLimit block.
A test pins the doc rate-limit table to rateLimitConfigs.
The API contract version is 2026-09-17 and the minimum supported equals it; callers naming an older version get CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED, callers naming none are served.
Every surface sends x-agi-surface, x-agi-client-version and x-agi-api-version; each app has its own header builder, and the CLI's is a Rust copy.

Rust protocol types are exported by ts-rs through a test and a staging directory into packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol (654 files); pnpm generate:protocol-types writes and pnpm check:protocol-types compares.
The public OpenAPI file is hand-kept, version 1.0.0, with 29 paths and three credential schemes (session bearer, sk_ API key, agiadm_ workspace key).
withErrorHandler wraps routes, assigns a request id, hides unsafe error text behind generic messages, and stamps API version headers.
Errors are classed once (authentication, entitlement, rate_limit, quota, provider_unavailable and others) with retryable and suggestedAction fields.
Managed cloud clients are factories taking a fetch function; Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome call them, while the CLI uses Rust clients guarded by golden fixtures.
/api/v1/providers/{providerId}/stream is retired and answers 410 CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REQUIRED.
Concurrent managed turns are capped per plan by BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS.maxConcurrentTurns, separate from request-rate limits; usage over quota answers 402 insufficient_quota.
Routes that skip the account and tenant gate are listed with reasons in route-authentication.json and enforced by check:route-account-gate.
Rate-limit ceilings can be scaled up only outside production; production ignores the env scale and logs an error.
The public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so route changes reach it on web deploy; the Tauri build reaches Rust only through registered commands.
Contract ownership moved from packages/services/src/cloud-contracts to packages/contracts/cloud-contracts and a guard enforces the new home.
check:route-shared-contracts requires client-called routes to import a shared contract; legacy routes sit in a baseline that only shrinks.
The api.agiworkforce.com alias is described as not release-verified until a production deploy and live authenticated request are recorded.
Redis fail-closed behavior: with the shared limiter unavailable in production, fail-closed keys refuse with 429 and fail-open keys pass.
Only Cloud (Managed Cloud) turns reach api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions; Local and BYOK never do.
The route has maxDuration 300 s; the tool-loop and provider stream budget is 240 s (300 s minus a 60 s teardown reserve).
The whole turn has a 40 s first-token budget; each provider attempt gets 25 s, clamped to what is left of the 40 s. Each tool call has a 120 s deadline.
Request order in the route: auth gate (rate limit, identity, CSRF, terms, age, subscription), turn slot, policy and spend gates, processRequest, secret gate, provider-start mark, dispatch.
The user message is persisted before any model call; if that fails the route returns 503 user_message_persistence_failed and sends no model request.

Context building (account memory, past chats, project files) runs in resolveInteractiveTurnContext; a loader failure continues without that source, but a project context failure fails closed with no model request.
Memory is off for temporary chats and, on the API surface, only on when memory_enabled is true; past-chat recall is never used on the API surface.
Provider dispatch goes through the ADAPTER_PROVIDERS table to adapters in packages/ai/providers/*; a provider not in the table fails as unsupported-provider and the reservation is refunded.

Failover rotates only before the first byte reaches the client, only on availability-class errors (and credential rejection), never on billing, safety or content-blocked; a pinned model is never answered by a different model; all attempts share one reservation settled at the serving model's price.
Same-route retry happens first: up to 2 attempts (overload class has its own limit), never for auth or context-overflow errors, and only while the 40 s first-token budget has room.

Tool loop default step budgets are 10 (chat), 100 (AGI Work), 20 (caller tools); exhausting the budget pauses the run on a checkpoint rather than killing it; manual approval saves a signed checkpoint before emitting x_tool_approval_request.

Tool-loop and research turns start on the durable Workflow transport unless AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS is off, the breaker is open, or the first event misses a 500 ms default budget (AGI_DURABLE_FIRST_EVENT_BUDGET_MS); then they fall back to an inline stream with the same wire. Plain chat is always inline.
A detached durable stream ends the connection with x_run_detached (reason function_budget) while the run continues; the web client and mobile follow the run by id.

Managed usage uses one reservation per turn (table managed_usage_requests) keyed by the Idempotency-Key; settlement bills list price of the serving model and records the served route's price as provider cost; failed turns bill zero; a stopped turn bills on delivered text only.

The server saves the assistant row (upsert by client-supplied assistant_message_id) at stream end, marking cancelled or incomplete turns truncated with reason stream_cancelled; temporary conversations are not saved.
The web client also saves its own copy through api:POST /api/chat/conversations/{id}/messages; a server-side edit guard returns a content-changed conflict, and a failed save marks metadataNotSaved.

Titles are two-stage: a truncated first-message title is set synchronously by the server; a fire-and-forget utility-model call (6 words, 24 output tokens, via managed route admission, cache and a conversation_title usage lease) replaces it; failures keep the truncated one.

Concurrent managed turns are capped per plan (billing catalog maxConcurrentTurns); over the cap returns 429 concurrent_turn_limit_reached and a limiter outage returns 503 concurrency_limiter_unavailable.

Local turns are decided from the model id prefix local:, run through a desktop-host bridge command local_chat_start (Ollama or LM Studio), accept text only, and never call the route, reserve compute or persist to the cloud.
The public Electron Desktop refuses on-device inference commands for chat; its local coding sessions use the bundled CLI.
Own-key (BYOK) is available in CLI by policy, permitted but marked unwired for VS Code in the harness catalog, and absent on Web, Desktop chat, Mobile and Chrome.
A conversation that holds Local turns cannot be continued with a cloud model from the web client, so local content is never uploaded.

Auth gate: a missing subscription is the Free website plan; a lapsed paid plan is served as Free; an unpaid enterprise plan gets 403 subscription_inactive; terms and adult-eligibility checks apply to session callers.
The route comment claims every managed turn starts durable; code shows only tool-loop and research branches try the durable transport.
Secret-looking content is blocked (400 secret_detected, reservation refunded) or redacted before dispatch, and the count is returned in a header.

Account tool-approval policy has three values: ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous. A signed-in cloud account with nothing stored defaults to autonomous; ask_every_time is the fail-closed fallback.
A workspace that forbids autonomous approvals drops a member from autonomous to ask_every_time (not to read-only); every workspace the user belongs to must allow autonomy.
The per-call gate is a nine-row ranked table; escalation to a person becomes a deny in an unattended run that cannot pause.
Even under autonomous, irreversible writes, deletes, external sends and shell commands still ask; web search, page fetch and sandboxed code are flagged to run without asking under read-only.
Device steps and browser commands are never auto-approved by the account policy; when a cleared device host is present the server gate allows device steps, and the device holds its own grant.

Step limits differ: chat 10, caller-driven 20, Work 100, Cloud Code 12/24/48 (default 24), 8 device steps per pause, 32 tool calls per step; Work plans hold 6 planned steps in the agent plan and up to 32 stored steps.
Web search uses a Perplexity search backend, returns at most 5 results per call and 3 calls per turn (10 in Work).
Free plan web search is capped at 20 calls per rolling 30 days; paid plans and automated callers (API, CLI, VS Code, scheduled, Work, research) are charged to managed credits per call.

Code execution uses our E2B sandbox only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, an E2B key and a compute price are set; otherwise a capable model gets its provider's own hosted code tool, so code then runs at the model provider.
Sandbox limits by plan: Free 2 sandboxes and 60 minutes; Basic 5; Premium 10; Max, Ultra and Enterprise 20; paid runs up to 24 hours; Local and BYOK 0.
create_office_file produces docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf and csv on the server, can edit an attached docx or xlsx, with a 20 MiB generated file cap.
The image tools are offered only on web, desktop, mobile and chrome surfaces, only on Premium and above, and only when image storage and a default provider are configured.
AGI Work needs Premium or higher; the server answers agi_work_plan_required otherwise. Work mode forces streaming and turns search, fetch and code on unless the goal excludes them.
Scheduled tasks are run by Vercel cron every 15 minutes; the run executes inside the cron request in waves of 10 (max 50 per sweep, 55 s budget).
Scheduled task caps by plan: Free, Local and BYOK 0; Basic 3; Premium 5; Max 15; Ultra 25; Team 10; Enterprise custom. Create is refused above the cap.
A paused scheduled run waits for approval for 24 hours, then stops; retries allowed 0 to 5 with backoff from 60 seconds to 24 hours.
Scheduled runs use a managed cloud route and are cloud-only; the CLI returns NotManaged outside managed cloud mode.
Event trigger sources are gmail, slack, google_calendar, github and connector; at most 50 triggers per account and 30 runs per hour / 720 per day per owner.
Connectors are in the coming_soon state, so Gmail and Google Calendar triggers are refused at creation and connector tools are not generally live.
Cloud Code agent classifies each shell command as safe, requires approval, or denied (sudo, curl, wget, git push, hard reset, credential files); Basic and up include it.

Chrome browser actions call our cloud model (never a local one), require a model with tools, vision and streaming, and have four permission modes: ask, auto (default), full, yolo; payment, purchase, publish, upload, sensitive-site and similar actions always ask.
Desktop computer use works only on macOS through a signed input helper, needs the computer.use grant, and stops on a stop shortcut or any user mouse or keyboard input.
Artifacts render in a separate-origin sandbox page whose CSP blocks all network connections; published artifacts live in published_artifacts under an unguessable URL.

Custom MCP servers must use HTTPS and resolve to a public host, with no embedded credentials. The count is limited by the plan's customMcpServers limit.
A tool call through /api/connectors/<id>/mcp checks allow, ask or deny and a critical risk tier, returns approvalRequired until approved, and writes an audit event.

The directory snapshot merges the official MCP registry crawl with first-party.json (32 entries) and vendor-directory.json (401 entries); hand-checked.json is empty.
Plugins install through three paths. Built-in packs go to plugin_installations. Directory and own-marketplace plugins go to plugin_marketplace_installations.
A directory plugin is web-installable only if it ships a skill and declares no hooks, language server or stdio MCP server.
skills-lock.json lists 113 skills (64 product, 49 developer). Only product skills reach customers through the managed skill catalog.
Editing any skill file fails CI until the lock is regenerated with node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate. Skills must not be installed with npx skills add.
The Rust MCP crate speaks protocol 2026-07-28 and four legacy versions, over stdio, SSE and HTTP. It is used by desktop (Tauri) and CLI.
CLI MCP OAuth tokens go in the OS keyring; the old JSON file is read only for migration. Desktop encrypts them into its settings database.
The Slack app is installed per workspace. The bot token is sealed with purpose slack-bot-token. Events arrive at /api/webhooks/slack, verified by signing secret.
The Slack assistant refuses a user whose plan lacks slack_app (reply slack_plan_required) and refuses task mode without agi_work.
Slack bot scopes the code requests: app_mentions:read, channels:history, chat:write, groups:history, im:history, reactions:write, users:read. Approvals expire after 24 hours.
The Slack app is configured only when the signing secret, client id and secret, app origin and token storage are all present.
Mobile finishes connector OAuth through an app-return route that calls oauth/complete. The web callback hands state, code and iss to the app when the app started the flow.
The Chrome extension has no connector client. It reads the canUseConnectors capability and shows the coming-soon state, and it exposes page-declared WebMCP tools.

Chat attachments upload through api:POST /api/uploads/presign, a PUT to private storage (or a same-origin relay api:PUT /api/uploads/chat-attachment/put), then api:POST /api/uploads/chat-attachment/complete, which scans and seals the file.
Upload scanning has three layers in scanUploadBytes: structural inspection, credential scan, and an external ClamAV call to UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL with a 15 second timeout; only {safe:true} passes.
In production the external scanner is required unless UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false; an unconfigured production deployment refuses every upload (fail closed).
The scanner is our own ClamAV service (Fly.io) that streams bytes to clamd and never writes them to disk; it refuses encrypted and too-complex archives; unauthenticated calls get 401.
Inline chat file ceiling is 25 MiB per file and per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files; clients without the handshake (CLI) use 12 MiB and 10 files.

Large chat files (up to 500 MiB) use a resumable multipart upload under /api/files/uploads, an intake pipeline with a protocol 2 source scan, and are available only on paid plans when CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED is on and the scanner answers the capability probe.
Free plan: 5 attachment uploads per UTC day, 500 MiB storage, no large chat files. Paid tiers: unlimited uploads, large files on, storage 4 GiB (basic) up to 100 GiB (max_15x).
Storage used is one number shared by the Library and project knowledge files, computed over table:media_assets and table:project_knowledge_files; temporary-chat files are mostly excluded.

Files live in S3-compatible object storage, default Cloudflare R2, configured by AGI_STORAGE_* (legacy CLOUDFLARE_R2_*); the private bucket must differ from the public bucket and holds chat attachments and project knowledge.
The Library is a view over table:media_assets served by api:GET /api/library; delete is a soft delete with 30 day recovery and a nightly purge cron at 04:00; permanent delete respects legal holds.

api:GET /api/files/{id} serves bytes with no-store caching and nosniff; HTML, SVG and XML types are forced to download as octet-stream; files over 30 MiB (video 256 MiB) are not served inline; downloads spend the monthly allowance.

Scripted artifacts render in infrastructure/sandbox/index.html on the separate origin named by NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN; the page accepts messages only from an exact allowlist of parent origins and only from its own parent window.
The sandbox's response CSP sets connect-src 'none', no forms, scripts only from itself and pinned CDNs, and frame-ancestors limited to our web hosts.
Without a configured sandbox origin the web falls back to a same-document srcDoc iframe with sandbox allow-scripts allow-modals, where scripts may not run and React artifacts need the origin.
The Tauri desktop build serves the same renderer from an artifact:// scheme compiled into the binary; the public Electron desktop shows the hosted web app.

Publishing uses api:POST /api/artifacts/publish; kinds html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code; content up to 1,000,000 characters; 200 publications per user; 24-character token; URL path /shared-artifact/<token>; html, react and mermaid render in the sandbox.
Publication runs the external-sharing gate, usage-policy moderation and outbound content inspection; a publication that uses connectors cannot be made public.
Anonymous read of a published artifact needs visibility public plus the token; organization visibility is limited to members with a grant row.

AI and connector calls from artifacts go through api:POST /api/artifacts/runtime/... and are allowed only for artifacts made in a managed-cloud chat, subject to an AI switch and concurrent-turn limits.
Project knowledge uploads require a SHA-256; older clients get 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.
Chat attachments are checked against a hash denylist of known illegal media and a workspace data-loss policy before storage.
docs/security/upload-scanning.md says no web code calls the scanner's /v2 routes yet, but source-scan-client.ts and chat-file-intake/steps.ts do.
Account export is api:GET/POST /api/user/export; media inside it is given as authenticated download links, not inline bytes.
A guard script lists every route that stores upload bytes and the files that finish them, and requires each to inspect the bytes.
Mobile local mode parses documents on the phone with a device-memory ceiling and no plan count; cloud mode uses the server limits from the handshake.
Whether production currently has the sandbox origin, the scanner and large files switched on is not established by any file read.
Instruction hierarchy has six layers, highest first: system, developer, project, personalized, memory, untrusted_context. Memory and untrusted_context are reference-only.
Project instructions outrank the account's custom instructions; a losing instruction layer is 'narrowed', a losing memory layer is 'ignored', a losing untrusted layer is 'quoted'.
Project knowledge files map to the untrusted_context layer; project instructions to project; account memory, past chats and sibling project chats to memory.
The stable system preamble is ordered system, developer(study), project, personalized (custom instructions then chat instruction); recalled and untrusted blocks go after the cache boundary.
Memory is off by default for a user: capabilities.memory must be true. generateFromHistory defaults on, searchPastChats off, includeSensitiveTopics off, tool-assisted generation off.
A temporary chat reads no account memory, no past chats and learns nothing; no context manifest is stored for it.
A temporary chat cannot be in a project; conversation create rejects projectId with isTemporary, and the policy file states the refusal text.
Temporary chat rows are purged after 30 days by a cron, unless a legal hold applies.
Temporary chats keep custom instructions by default; a 'personalized' toggle (default on) turns them off by sending personalization=false, which also forces memory_enabled=false.
Memory read caps per turn: 30 memories, 1,000 chars each, 8,000 total, from up to 500 candidates ranked by pinned then relevance.
Project limits: name 200, description 2,000, instructions 10,000 chars; up to 40 knowledge files; 16,000 chars per file and 48,000 total in a turn.
Custom instructions text is capped at 2,000 chars; 'about you' at 1,500; preferred name 60; work description 120.

A project can opt out of account custom instructions and style (uses_account_instructions, uses_account_style) and out of global memory (uses_global_memory); memory written in a project is project-scoped.
The workspace policy row governs memory, past chats, connector results and web results; a missing or unreadable row closes everything.

Image jobs are durable: up to 3 attempts on one reservation, claim 180 s, lease 3600 s; with async true the route returns 202 and the client polls /api/media/image/status; the status call also re-drives a due job.

Image requests accept prompt up to 4000 characters, up to 4 images (1 for the Gemini image API), up to 3 edit reference images, and operations generate, edit, inpaint, outpaint, variation; only the OpenAI image API supports edits.
Video requests accept a prompt up to 2000 characters, clip 2 to 30 s (default 4), up to 4 candidates each billed as its own job, and optional first-frame or reference images (not both).
Video is processed by a durable Vercel Workflow; the client polls /api/media/video/status (web and Chrome every 5 s for 5 min); OpenRouter can call a signed webhook.
Prompt moderation and uploaded-image hash and structure checks run before any billing reservation or provider call, so a refused image request is never charged.
Base rate limits per minute: image 10, video 5, video status 30, transcription 20, read-aloud 30, live session create 10; all but video status fail closed.

Mobile dictation runs fully on the device through expo-speech-recognition with on-device recognition required; mobile read-aloud uses server speech in Cloud conversations and the device voice otherwise.

The rate limiter has 147 named buckets; each is fail-closed or fail-open, and production throws at import if shared store credentials are missing.

vercel.json defines 47 cron jobs; health-probe runs every 10 minutes and evaluate-slo-burn at :05 and :35.

API errors are wrapped by handleError. The message is replaced by a generic one (for example 'Internal server error', 'Upstream service error') unless the error is user-safe or its code is in SAFE_TO_EXPOSE_CODES, which includes CREDIT_REQUIRED, SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, VALIDATION_ERROR, MFA_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE and all DenialErrorCode values.

Three code families exist: ErrorCode (with HTTP map), DenialErrorCode (who refused: user, organization, workspace, role, device policy, unsupported by model/provider/route/surface/OS/region, upgrade/seat/entitlement/quota, provider degraded/unavailable, offline, maintenance, feature lifecycle) and DomainErrorCode (storage, search, tool, connector, sandbox, safety, deleted).

Provider failures are classified by classifyError into categories (aborted, api_timeout, rate_limit, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, context_overflow, max_output, tool_validation, invalid_model, invalid_input, unsupported_input, media_too_large, auth, billing_exhausted, quota_exhausted, safety, content_blocked, empty_response, connection, pause_turn, server_error, client_error, unknown) and turned into user copy by mapClassifiedUpstreamError.

billing_exhausted (our provider account out of funds) is deliberately kept separate from auth and is shown as HTTP 503 code provider_billing_exhausted, so the user is not shown a payment error and the turn is not rotated onto another paid provider.
A spent shared free model pool yields code free_allowance_exhausted (429) with copy saying it is not a limit on the user's account; other quota exhaustion yields provider_quota_exhausted.

Managed usage refusals: 402 insufficient_credits, 402 extra_usage_required, 429 artifact_runtime_limit_reached, 429 rolling_five_hour_limit_reached, 429 rolling_weekly_limit_reached, 429 flagship_weekly_limit_reached, 503 billing_unavailable, and 409 idempotency_in_progress, idempotency_replay and idempotency_conflict.
Clients decide what a quota code looks like (upgrade button, reset time, suggest standard model, cleared by credits) through classifyManagedQuotaErrorCode and the MANAGED_QUOTA_BLOCKS table.
Managed allowances come from MANAGED_USAGE_LIMITS per plan tier. The local-only and byok tiers have zero managed credits, so usage-limit errors apply only to managed cloud turns.
Free allowance sits above Basic in several windows. This is an open owner decision.
Stated waits in user copy are only used when a provider or server supplied Retry-After; values under 1 second or over 86,400 seconds are dropped.
A failure after answer text has started (connection, timeout, server error, unknown) is shown as stream_interrupted with the text 'The response stopped part way through...'.
The adapter's structured classification is read before any message text, so a user-chosen file name cannot decide whether a turn is retried or rotated.
Chat attachment limits live in chat-attachment-policy.json: 25 MiB per file, 25 MiB per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files, with a lower withoutHandshake set (12 MiB, 12 MiB, 12 MiB, 10 files).

The relay upload PUT refuses empty bodies and bodies over the limit with validation errors, refuses a missing token with 403, and fails with an internal error if private object storage is not configured. Presign URLs live 300 seconds.
Presign answers 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED to an old client that sends a project-source upload without the content-binding field.
Memory sync refuses a client whose sync protocol is below the minimum with a client-update-required error, and a client newer than the server with a validation error. Pull is capped at 1000 memories.
Mobile shows the toast 'Cloud changes haven't synced.' with a Retry action when sync is in the error state while online, signed in and in cloud mode.
